title: last-mile-smart-dispatch-poc-pricing-and-workshop-notes
content:
Executive summary:

This document captures the scope, technical approach, workshop plan, and a first-pass pricing/packaging sketch for a Last-Mile Smart Dispatch POC with CourierCo (customer). Goal: validate a Redwood-powered hybrid inference workflow that reduces driver idle time and improves ETA accuracy by combining embedding-based reranking for route suggestions with a streaming chat interface for drivers.

Why this POC matters:
- CourierCo suffers unpredictable ETAs (5-12% late deliveries) driven by dynamic traffic and nondeterministic routing decisions.
- We will show how Redwood inference (low-latency models + routing policies + caching) can be integrated into their dispatch system to produce near-real-time re-ranks and short explanations delivered to drivers over a lightweight mobile SDK.

Primary objectives and success metrics:
- Technical objective: Demonstrate sub-200ms median latency for single-turn route reranking requests at 10 qps sustained in the edge region (US-West) with a 99th percentile < 600ms during 1-minute bursts.
- Product objective: Reduce average route selection time per driver by 40% and improve ETA prediction MAPE by at least 12% on the sampled dataset.
- Business objective: Produce a clear cost-per-interaction model (hosted vs dedicated vs private) that maps to operational unit economics for 5k–50k daily driver interactions.

Stakeholders:
- CourierCo: Head of Dispatch (Primary Sponsor) and Mobile Lead (integration owner)
- Redwood: Solutions Eng lead (Maya Chen), Applied ML support (Priya Rao), Infra/Serving runtime contact (Evan Morales)

Scope of the POC (6 weeks, narrow):
1) Data & integration: one-week data extraction workshop + sample export (delivery logs, historical GPS traces, routing decisions). Minimal PII; tokenized driver IDs only.
2) Models: 2 model flavors: a lightweight reranker (quantized L2-embedding hybrid) for candidate routes and a small instruction-tuned model (for driver messaging and short explanations). Use curated open model from Redwood model catalog (Model-XQ-7B-quant) as baseline.
3) Serving: Deploy on Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2 for deterministic latency; enable prefix/KV caching for repeated route prefixes and workload-aware continuous batching.
4) Integration: Mobile SDK integration for streaming responses (low-bandwidth friendly), and REST webhook for dispatch system to request re-ranks.
5) Observability & metrics: Redwood Console dashboard with token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency traces, and a small set of custom evals comparing ETA vs ground truth.
6) Deliverables: deployment runbook, integration guide, perf report, cost model, and a go/no-go decision brief.

Technical approach (high level):
- Candidate generation remains in-house (CourierCo routing engine) -> produce top-10 route candidates per delivery.
- Reranking: send candidate set + recent telemetry to Redwood API endpoint. Use model variants and canary rollout to validate quality. Prefetch KV cache for common prefixes to reduce cold-start costs for morning peaks.
- Streaming: drivers receive streaming clarifications and short guidance (function-calling like instructions for ETA updates). Mobile SDK uses chunked streaming to show partial suggestion ASAP.
- Fallbacks: policy-based routing -> on Dedicated capacity pressure, fallback to a smaller quantized model hosted in a secondary region or to a deterministic rule-based comparator.

Workshop plan (detailed):
- Week 0 (Kickoff, 2-hour): Alignment on success metrics, data availability checklist, security/PII review. Attendees: CourierCo dispatch, mobile, infra, Redwood SE, Redwood security.
- Week 1 (Data workshop, 4-hour): Data mapping session (fields, retention, sampling) + extraction script template.
- Week 2 (Model & infra deep-dive, 3-hour): Selection of model variant, quantization options, and Dedicated sizing exercise.
- Week 3 (Integration workshop, 3-hour): Mobile SDK demo, API contract, retry/backoff semantics, and logging/tracing setup.
- Week 4 (Load prep & smoke tests, remote 2-hour): Define synthetic load and edge-case scenarios; run small smoke tests.
- Week 5 (Perf run & review, remote 3-hour): Full perf run and analysis; adjust batching, cache TTLs.
- Week 6 (Closeout, 2-hour): Handover, cost model walkthrough, recommended next steps for productionization.

Estimated timeline (6 weeks):
- Total calendar time: 6 weeks from kickoff. Key milestones: data export ready (end of week 1), dev integration (end of week 3), perf run (week 5), findings and recommendations (week 6).

Resource & role assumptions:
- Redwood: 1 SE (lead) allocated 40% for 6 weeks, 1 Applied ML engineer 20% for model tuning, 1 Infra/DevOps 20% for Dedicated provisioning and runbook.
- CourierCo: 1 integration engineer full-time for 2–3 weeks; dispatch SME available ad-hoc.

Pricing sketch (first-pass):
- Professional services (redwood SE + ML + infra): 16 onsite/remote consultant days (estimate) allocated as: SE lead 10d, ML 4d, Infra 2d. Rate: $2,100/day (standard SE day rate). Professional services subtotal: $33,600.
- Dedicated capacity (POC configuration, 6 weeks): Recommended: 1x g5.2x (or equivalent) Dedicated slot with burst policy to 2x for peaks. POC price: $9,000 for 6 weeks (includes priority scheduling and monitoring).
- Hosted usage (if preferred instead of Dedicated): estimate $3,200 for 6 weeks at projected qps and token volumes (note: generally higher tail latency).
- Optional private deployment deposit (for evaluation only): one-time $45,000 (covers private control plane access, minimal on-prem packaging for isolated testing).
- Travel & misc: $2,000 (on-site workshop day if requested).
- Total POC cost (recommended path with Dedicated): Professional services + Dedicated + travel = ~$44.6k. Optional private add-on would be +$45k.

Acceptance criteria (go/no-go):
- Performance: median latency <200ms and 99th <600ms under target load.
- Quality: reranker improves ETA MAPE by >=12% on holdout sample and driver selection time reduced by >=30% in pilot cohort.
- Integration: mobile SDK streaming works end-to-end with <1s time-to-first-byte for partial suggestions in 90% of interactions.
- Economics: projected per-interaction cost (hosted/dedicated) meets CourierCo threshold (TBD during week 1).

Key risks and mitigations:
- Data quality/availability: Risk: GPS traces are sparse or inconsistent. Mitigation: use synthetic augmentation + focus on peak corridors first.
- Cold-start model latency during morning surge: Mitigation: pre-warming, prefix/KV caching, and preload common route prefixes overnight.
- Mobile network variability: Mitigation: adopt ultra-short partial outputs and robust retry/backoff in SDK; allow client-side fallback to last-known good route.
- Security/compliance: Risk: CourierCo requires strict audit trails. Mitigation: enable Redwood audit logs and KMS integration in Dedicated; sign-off during kickoff.

Open questions for CourierCo to answer prior to kickoff:
- Can customer provide a sampled daily export (last 90 days) with the following minimal fields: route-id, candidate coordinates, timestamps, selected-route, actual-arrival?
- Does the mobile app allow introducing SDK-based streaming with background network privileges?
- Latency SLO target: is 200ms median acceptable, or do they require tighter constraints?

Next steps (proposal flow):
1) Send this sketch to CourierCo for initial feedback and priorities (2 business days).
2) Lock in resource availability and finalize SOW with exact day counts and milestone payments (end of week).
3) Schedule kickoff workshop and request sample data export.

Notes & errata (working):
- This is a draft pricing sketch; final numbers will be refined after the Week 2 Dedicated sizing exercise and after we see token volumes from a day sample.
- Consider including Redwood Optimize in the pilot to automatically suggest batching/caching configs during week 5 perf run (adds $1,500 optional fee).

Appendix A: Quick perf knobs to try during perf run:
- Turn on KV cache TTL to 30 minutes for morning corridors.
- Adjust batch size target to keep p99 CPU under 75% (monitor Redwood Console).
- Canary route policies: 70/30 split between quantized reranker and full model to observe quality delta.
